review_candidates.description: Position Summary Job Type: Full-time | Location: Ft Worth, TX | Department : Operations | Reporting to: Head of Procurement | Work Location Type: #remote or #hybrid IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC. With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in. The Director, Regional Project Procurement leads tactical, project-level procurement execution across the company's U.S. data center construction portfolio. Reporting to the Vice President, Data Center Procurement, this role owns the on-the-ground purchasing engine that translates category strategies and master agreements into site-ready materials and services: issuing purchase orders, managing regional supplier relationships, resolving field procurement issues in real time, driving day-to-day buying discipline across multiple concurrent construction projects, and reporting procurement status across projects to key stakeholders. This is an execution-focused leadership role that sits at the intersection of strategic sourcing, construction project management, and field operations. Success requires a leader who can build and manage a regional procurement organization, hold suppliers and internal stakeholders accountable to schedule and cost commitments, and rapidly resolve the tactical issues that inevitably arise across a fast-moving, multi-site data center build program. Key Responsibilities Tactical & Project-Level Procurement Execution: Lead all tactical (PO-level) procurement activity for assigned regions/projects, converting approved category strategies and master supply agreements into timely purchase orders. Own the buy-to-delivery cycle for construction materials, equipment, and site services, ensuring purchase orders align with construction schedules, budgets, and specifications. Manage day-to-day supplier communication for order confirmation, order changes, expediting, and issue resolution at the project and site level. Establish and enforce standardized tactical procurement processes, approval workflows, and PO governance across all regional teams. Drive resolution of field procurement escalations (material shortages, quality issues, delivery delays) in partnership with construction, engineering, and logistics teams. Regional Program & Supplier Management: Build and maintain regional supplier relationships for trade contractors, equipment vendors, and local/regional material suppliers supporting active builds. Monitor regional supplier performance (on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness) and drive corrective action plans where performance falls short. Support project-level bid packages, quote comparisons, and award recommendations for regionally sourced scopes of work and materials. Partner with Strategic Sourcing/Category Management to provide field-level market intelligence and supplier feedback that informs national category strategy and master agreements. Manage regional procurement budgets and track project-level spend against approved project budgets, flagging variances early. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Schedule Alignment: Partner closely with Construction Project Managers and Site Superintendents to align procurement activities with construction sequencing and critical-path milestones. Collaborate with Warehousing, Inventory Control, and Logistics teams to ensure tactical purchase orders translate into on-time, on-site material delivery. Work with Legal and Contracts teams to execute purchase orders and short-form agreements within approved contract terms and delegation-of-authority limits. Provide regular reporting to the VP, Data Center Procurement on regional procurement status, risks, spend, and schedule impacts across the project portfolio. Own the procurement input into recurring project governance forums for each assigned project — including weekly management reviews, EPC/owner-contractor meetings, and project status presentations — covering material and equipment delivery status, long-lead item tracking, open escalations, and cost/schedule impacts. Consolidate project-level inputs from Regional Project Procurement Managers, site buyers, and expediters into a single accurate procurement submission for each forum, delivered on the required cadence and in the required format. Represent procurement in weekly management, EPC, and project review calls, presenting status and responding to questions on delivery risk, supplier performance, and mitigation plans. Team Leadership & Organizational Development: Build, lead, and develop a team of regional procurement managers, tactical buyers, and expediters aligned to active and planned construction regions. Establish staffing plans that scale the tactical procurement organization in line with the pace and geographic spread of the data center build pipeline. Define KPIs and performance standards for the tactical procurement team (PO cycle time, on-time issuance, cost savings/avoidance, supplier performance). Champion consistent tools, systems (P2P/ERP), and processes across regions to enable scalability and reduce variability in procurement execution. Establish and maintain standardized procurement reporting templates, dashboards, and data sources so project updates are consistent across projects and regions and traceable back to PO, delivery, and spend data. Requirements & Qualifications: Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Construction Management, Business, Engineering, or related field (Master's degree preferred). 12+ years of progressive procurement experience, including significant experience in tactical/project procurement supporting large-scale construction or capital projects, with 5+ years in a senior leadership role. Direct experience supporting data center, hyperscale, industrial, or other mission-critical construction programs. Strong track record managing regional or multi-site procurement teams and driving execution discipline across concurrent, fast-paced projects. Solid understanding of construction procurement processes, purchase order/contract fundamentals, and project schedule/cost drivers. Proficiency with ERP/P2P systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Coupa) and project management or construction management platforms. Demonstrated ability to build and lead teams across multiple U.S. regions, including remote and site-based staff. Willingness to travel domestically up to 40-50% to active construction sites and regional offices. Preferred Qualifications Experience specifically within data center, colocation, or hyperscale construction procurement organizations. CPSM, CPSD, or equivalent procurement/supply chain certification. Familiarity with electrical, mechanical, and general trades scopes typical of data center construction (switchgear, generators, UPS, cooling, structural steel, etc.). Experience partnering with Strategic Sourcing/Category Management organizations to translate national strategy into regional execution. Physical Requirements & Work Environment Primarily a site-based role with frequent, recurring travel to active construction sites and regional field offices. Ability to walk active construction sites, including exposure to outdoor conditions and standard site PPE requirements. Job Benefits At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth. Compensation Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and market data for the region. Total Compensation package may be inclusive of annual incentive bonus, equity (long-term incentive). review_candidates.title: Counter-Terrorism Officer (S)
review_candidates.description: Background This position is open for secondment only and participating States are kindly reminded that all costs in relation to an assignment at the Secretariat must be borne by their authorities. The duties and requirements of this seconded (S) position correspond to a P3-level role in the UN common system. Candidates should, prior to applying, verify with their respective nominating authority to which extent financial remuneration and/or benefit packages will be offered. Please note that seconded staff members in the OSCE Secretariat and Institutions are not entitled to a Board and Lodging Allowance payable by the Organization. The OSCE has a comprehensive approach to security that encompasses politico-military, economic and environmental, and human aspects. It therefore addresses a wide range of security-related concerns, including arms control, confidence- and security-building measures, human rights, combating human trafficking, national minorities, democratization, policing strategies, counter-terrorism and economic and environmental activities. All 57 participating States enjoy equal status, and decisions are taken by consensus on a politically, but not legally binding basis. The OSCE Secretariat in Vienna assists the Chairpersonship in its activities, and provides operational and administrative support to the field operations, and, as appropriate, to other institutions. OSCE Ministerial Council Decision MC.DEC/9/11 of 7 December 2011 established the Transnational Threats Department (TNTD) as part of the OSCE Secretariat in Vienna, Austria. TNTD plays a key role as the focal point of OSCE-wide programmatic activities aiming at countering transnational threats and ensuring the co-ordination and coherence of action across all three OSCE dimensions among all executive structures, while respecting their mandates. TNTD comprises the Co-ordination Cell, the Action against Terrorism Unit, the Border Security and Management Unit and the Strategic Police Matters Unit. The Action against Terrorism Unit (ATU), operating under the Transnational Threats Department (TNTD) within the OSCE Secretariat, serves as a pivotal element in the organization's counter-terrorism efforts. Led by the Head of the Unit (H/TNTD/ATU) who reports directly to the TNTD Co-ordinator, the ATU stands as the central node for information, co-ordination, and implementation of counter-terrorism activities. This unit embodies the OSCE's commitment to combating terrorism, as mandated by decisions from the Permanent and Ministerial Council meetings, especially in enforcing the “OSCE Consolidated Framework for the Fight against Terrorism” as per PC Decision No. 1063. Tasks And Responsibilities The incumbent, under the supervision of the Head of the ATU, plays a crucial role in advancing the Unit’s objectives in the fight against terrorism. As a key team member, the individual is responsible for monitoring and reporting on anti-terrorism developments, identifying areas for assistance, and formulating policy and project proposals. This role involves proposing actionable courses to supervisors, enhancing activity implementation, and mobilizing extra-budgetary funds. The incumbent’s contributions are not limited to team collaboration; they also extend to facilitating interactions among participating States, focusing on technical assistance and co-operation. This proactive engagement in project design and implementation underscores the individual's vital role in fostering collaborative efforts to combat terrorism. More specifically, the Counter-Terrorism Officer will be tasked with the following: Participating in the conception, development, implementation and the evaluation of OSCE counter-terrorism programmes or projects in line with the OSCE counter-terrorism commitments; monitoring programme/project development and implementation; at each stage of the process, identifying possible problems and issues to be addressed and proposing corrective actions; liaising with relevant parties and stakeholders, including national authorities and external experts; identifying and tracking follow-up actions; As a portfolio manager, following closely the developments occurring in a series of thematic areas pertaining to counter-terrorism and/or identified as key issues to the TNTD/ATU activities; With a strong focus on human rights, rule of law, and strong awareness on gendered aspects of violent extremism and terrorism, identify trends and possible gaps; and propose course of action; Capturing best practices and lessons learned; Facilitating their proper dissemination within the OSCE environment; Participating actively as a representative of the TNTD/ATU in counter-terrorism activities set up by other OSCE institutions and bodies, international and regional organizations as well as other stakeholders; Facilitating the co-ordination of the assigned portfolio activities with those developed by other OSCE Institutions and Field Operations; Reporting to the relevant OSCE bodies as required, including the Security Committee; Providing expert advice as requested by the Secretary General or the Chairman-in-Office through the Head of the Unit; Avoiding overlapping and duplication of work, identify, exploring and fostering synergies and complementarities between the ATU and possible project partners; Drawing on OSCE strength in terms of facilitation abilities and political visibility; Facilitating interaction between the participating States following PC Decision No. 1063 and other relevant OSCE documents, including bilateral technical assistance and co-operation in the assigned portfolio. Identify, together with the interested participating States, gaps, needs, requirements and resources for assistance in implementing counter-terrorism measures; Assisting in identifying possible additional tasking by the Permanent Council of the OSCE field presences in close co-operation and agreement with host governments; Assisting H//TNTD/ATU in providing guidance to fund managers of OSCE executive structures to facilitate the achievement of the established counter-terrorism goals; Performing other related duties as assigned. For more detailed information on the structure and work of the OSCE Secretariat, please see: Secretariat | Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Necessary Qualifications A first-level university degree in international relations, political science, criminology, international law, human rights, terrorism studies, security studies or a closely related field; A minimum of seven years (five years with a relevant second-level degree) of progressively responsible and relevant professional experience in political affairs, with a strong focus on human rights; Understanding of UN SCR 2242 and the women, peace and security agenda, and at least two years with international organizations and previous experience at the OSCE (Institutions/field operations) is a distinct asset; Solid understanding of the global counterterrorism framework and relevant OSCE documents and UN resolutions; Established relevant professional experience in human rights and rule of law; Established relevant experience in project management and donor relations; Experience liaising with a wide range of stakeholders, including high-level government and international organizations; Professional fluency in English with excellent communication (both oral and written) skills; Working knowledge of at least one other language from the OSCE region is an asset; Demonstrated gender awareness and sensitivity, and an ability to integrate a gender perspective into tasks and activities; Ability and willingness to work as a member of team, with people of different cultural, and religious backgrounds, different gender, and diverse political views, while maintaining impartiality and objectivity; Digital literacy to operate windows applications including word processing and email. If you wish to apply for this position, please use the OSCE's online application link found under https://vacancies.osce.org/ . If your participating State does not provide the option to apply online for seconded positions, you are kindly requested to submit your offline application form available at https://jobs.osce.org/resources/document/offline-application-form to the respective OSCE delegation whose address can be found at https://www.osce.org/contacts/delegations . The OSCE retains the discretion to re-advertise/re-post the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer an appointment with a modified job description or for a different duration. Only those candidates who are selected to participate in the subsequent stages of recruitment will be contacted. Please note that vacancies in the OSCE are open for competition only amongst nationals of participating States, please see https://www.osce.org/participating-states . The OSCE is committed to diversity and inclusion within its workforce, and encourages the nomination of qualified female and male candidates from all religious, ethnic and social backgrounds. The OSCE is a non-career organization committed to the principle of staff rotation; therefore, the maximum period of service in this post is 10 years. Candidates should be aware that OSCE officials shall conduct themselves at all times in a manner befitting the status of an international civil servant.
